The Savoy Male and Female College      51

    Commercial Art.—In addition to the academic courses described above, the Savoy College curriculum included at all times a complete commercial department, and through all of its years either maintained departments of music and art or cooperated informally with private teachers of these subjects with studios in the college buildings or adjoining the campus that work in these branches was regarded as an integral part of the curriculum by many of the parents. The commercial course—including bookkeeping, business arithmetic, and business penmanship—was conducted by President Halsel and his faculty in cooperation with visiting commercial teachers. They are Kyger and George Harshaw from about 1882 to 1884, when these two are listed in Grayson County as having labeled the Gale City Commercial School.³⁴ The next year (1884-1885) Mr. J. D. Warren is listed in The Plainsman Messenger as Principal of the Commercial Department and Mr. L. J. (Lee) Montgomery as well as being listed as Professor of Business Penmanship for the year 1886-1887. All the diplomas in Business Penmanship seem to have been offered on genuine sheepskin by the penmanship instructors of the advanced students.³⁵ The Art work included water color and oil painting and pencil sketching; instruction was, it can be estimated, from the scheduling for the degree course, at a half year each. The Art work included water color and oil painting and was priced at five dollars.
